title: Looker vs. Power BI: Which One Is Better In 2026?
summary: Looker vs Power BI in 2026: LookML vs DAX, sales-quoted Looker vs Power BI Pro at $14 a user, Gemini vs Copilot, plus Looker Studio vs Power BI.
body_markdown:
And if your real bottleneck is the queue of questions in front of your data team rather than the BI tool, switching platforms won't fix it. Still weighing more options? Our[Looker alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-alternatives) and[Looker vs Tableau](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-vs-tableau) comparisons cover the rest of the field, including[what Tableau costs](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-pricing) .


## Modeling: LookML vs Power BI semantic models and DAX


This is the real difference between the two tools, and it decides who on your team does the work.


### How Looker models data: LookML


LookML is Looker's modeling language. A developer defines views, dimensions, measures and the joins between them (an "Explore") once, in code, in a semantic layer Google describes as sitting "directly above your cloud data warehouse" ([Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker) ). At query time Looker writes the SQL from that LookML and runs it against your database, including for any tool that queries through Looker's API.


- **Who writes it:** only Developer users get LookML Development Mode, administration and the Looker API. Standard users can explore, run SQL Runner and build dashboards; Viewers can view, filter, drill and schedule ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ).
- **What it costs you:** an analytics engineer's time. LookML is code, and someone has to keep it current as tables change.
- **What you get back:** one definition of "active customer" that every dashboard, embedded app, Gemini answer and API caller inherits.


### How Power BI models data: semantic models and DAX


A Power BI semantic model holds tables, relationships and measures written in DAX. You build models in Power BI Desktop, Microsoft's free authoring app, then publish them to the Power BI service with a Pro or Premium Per User license ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ).


- **Limits by license:** Pro models are capped at 1 GB and refresh up to 8 times a day; Premium Per User raises that to 100 GB and 48 refreshes a day, and adds XMLA endpoint read/write, the interface external tools use to read and edit a model.
- **Who writes it:** analysts in a GUI, with DAX for the measures. The barrier to a first model is low.
- **The catch:** because a model is easy to start, it's easy to end up with one per report. Keeping "net revenue" identical across them takes discipline, or a shared model that every report connects to.


### Which approach suits your team


If you have, or plan to hire, an analytics engineer and want one governed layer for many tools, LookML is the stronger foundation. If your analysts live in Excel and need to ship reports this quarter, a Power BI semantic model gets you there faster. Our guide to the[Power BI semantic model](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-semantic-model) covers how to build one well, and[how Dot uses Power BI semantic models](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/how-dot-uses-your-power-bi-semantic-models) shows what a well-built model gives an AI tool to work with.


## Pricing: Looker vs Power BI (October 2026)


### Looker pricing


Looker charges a platform fee for running the instance and a license for each user. Every edition is an annual commitment (one-, two- or three-year terms) with the price listed as "call sales" ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ):


- **Standard:** for teams under 50 users; one production instance, 10 Standard and 2 Developer users, up to 1,000 query-based and 1,000 administrative API calls a month.
- **Enterprise:** enhanced security features for internal BI; up to 100,000 query-based and 10,000 administrative API calls a month.
- **Embed:** for external analytics and custom apps; up to 500,000 query-based and 100,000 administrative API calls a month.


Those API ceilings matter once you connect AI tools: an MCP client, a custom app or an AI analyst all make API calls, so check your edition's allowance before rolling one out to a large team. Conversational Analytics is metered separately in data tokens, with a monthly allowance that grows with each user and free promotional access through January 31, 2027; our[Looker AI guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) has the allowances and overage rates. For what third parties report Looker contracts cost, see our[Looker pricing breakdown](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-pricing) .


### Power BI pricing


Microsoft publishes its per-user prices ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) , checked October 29, 2026):


- **Free:** build reports in Power BI Desktop; sharing needs Pro or Premium.
- **Pro:** $14 per user a month, paid yearly. Included in Microsoft 365 E5 and Office 365 E5.
- **Premium Per User:** $24 per user a month, paid yearly, or a $14 step-up add-on for users who already have Pro or E5.
- **Embedded:** variable, priced by capacity.
- **Fabric capacity (F SKUs):** billed on Azure, pay-as-you-go or as an annual reservation priced about 40.5% below pay-as-you-go (Microsoft rounds it to ~41%). At $0.18 per capacity unit per hour in US West 2, the smallest F2 is $262.80 a month pay-as-you-go ([Microsoft Fabric blog](https://blog.fabric.microsoft.com/blog/announcing-microsoft-fabric-capacities-are-available-for-purchase) ). Our[Microsoft Fabric pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-fabric-pricing) covers every SKU.


Two footnotes drive most real bills: publishing to any capacity still needs a Pro license, and people can view reports without their own paid license only on F64 or P1 capacity and above.


Here's my arithmetic at list prices for 10 report builders and 200 viewers: 210 Pro seats come to $2,940 a month. F64 at $0.18 per CU-hour over a 730-hour month is $8,409.60 pay-as-you-go, or about $5,004 with the 40.5% reservation discount, plus $140 for the 10 builders' Pro seats. So at that size, seats are cheaper than capacity. Our[Power BI pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-pricing) works through more team sizes.


### Which costs less?


For a small team, Power BI almost always does, and you can prove it without talking to anyone: Looker's platform fee is a floor you pay before the first viewer logs in. Looker can make sense when it replaces a lot of hand-maintained SQL and many tools read from one model, but you won't know the number until Google quotes it.


## AI: Gemini in Looker vs Copilot and Fabric data agents


**Looker.** Conversational Analytics became generally available on November 14, 2025: users ask questions in plain language, follow up, and can ask how a number was calculated, and one agent can combine up to five Looker Explores ([Google Cloud blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/business-intelligence/looker-conversational-analytics-now-ga) ). Dashboard Agents and a Conversational Analytics API extend it ([Looker product page](https://cloud.google.com/looker) ). Everything is grounded in LookML, which is the point and the limit: Gemini answers well about what is modeled and can't reach what isn't. Details and costs are in our[Looker AI guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) , and the[Gemini in Looker vs Dot](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/looker-vs-dot) side-by-side compares features.


**Power BI.** Copilot answers questions, generates visuals and reports from a description, and writes summaries ([Power BI product page](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi) ), but it needs a paid Fabric capacity of F2 or above, or Premium P1 or above; a Pro or Premium Per User license alone doesn't turn it on ([Microsoft Fabric blog](https://blog.fabric.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/copilot-and-ai-capabilities-now-accessible-to-all-paid-skus-in-microsoft-fabric) ). Fabric data agents go further, generating SQL, DAX or KQL over lakehouses, warehouses and semantic models; they were reported generally available at FabCon in March 2026 ([Towards AI](https://pub.towardsai.net/fabric-data-agents-just-hit-ga-94f459c68dcc) ). See our[Power BI Copilot guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-copilot) and[Power BI Copilot comparison](https://www.getdot.ai/compare/powerbi-vs-dot) .


### MCP: Looker MCP server vs Power BI MCP servers


Both vendors offer Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers so AI assistants can query them directly. Looker has a managed MCP server built into the platform, plus the open-source MCP Toolbox for Databases for customer-hosted instances ([Looker docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/mcp) ). Microsoft recommends the generally available, read-only Fabric IQ MCP server for questions, keeps the older remote Power BI MCP server in preview, and offers a separate Authoring MCP server for editing models ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/developer/mcp/mcp-servers-overview) ). Setup and security for each are in our[Looker AI](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) and[Power BI MCP server](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-mcp-server) guides.


## Ecosystem fit


- **Looker** runs as a Google Cloud product: Cloud IAM single sign-on, Private Service Connect networking, customer-managed encryption keys, native BigQuery integration and unified billing ([Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker) ). It connects to other SQL databases too, but the fit is tightest on BigQuery.
- **Power BI** is part of Microsoft's Power Platform and Fabric. Reports share into Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and SharePoint ([Power BI](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi) ), and Fabric adds OneLake storage and Microsoft Purview governance ([Microsoft Fabric](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-fabric) ).


## Governance and security


- **Looker:** license type gates what each person can do, and LookML access filters tie row access to user attributes ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ).
- **Power BI:** semantic models carry security roles whose DAX filter expressions restrict rows per user. Fabric layers OneLake security, the OneLake catalog and Microsoft Purview on top ([Microsoft Fabric](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-fabric) ).


## Embedding


- **Looker** offers the Embed edition, with the largest API allowance, plus low-code iframe embedding, SDKs and the Conversational Analytics API for putting governed questions inside your product ([Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker) ).
- **Power BI Embedded** is priced by capacity and lets you brand reports as your own. Viewing without per-user licenses applies from F64 or P1 capacity, through the App Owns Data model ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ).


## Looker Studio (Data Studio) vs Power BI


Looker Studio is not Looker: it is Google's free report builder, renamed back to Data Studio in April 2026 ([Google Cloud blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/looker-studio-is-data-studio) ), with no LookML or semantic layer. If it's the tool you're replacing, see our Looker Studio (Data Studio) alternatives. Against Power BI, as of October 2026:


- **Price:** Data Studio is free for creators and viewers; Data Studio Pro (team content management, support and AI features) is $9 per user per project a month ([Data Studio](https://cloud.google.com/data-studio) ). Power BI sharing needs a $14 Pro seat for each builder and, below F64 capacity, each viewer.
- **Data:** Data Studio connects natively to Google Analytics, Google Ads, Sheets and BigQuery, plus 1,300+ community connectors; Power BI models data in DAX, with relationships and row-level security roles.
- **When each wins:** Data Studio for marketing and web reporting on Google data, shared at no cost; Power BI when you need a governed model or Microsoft 365.


## Where GetDot fits: an AI analyst on top of Looker or Power BI


Dot is an AI data analyst. It answers questions in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, the web app or any MCP client ([Dot MCP integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/mcp) ), and shows the query behind every number. It doesn't ask you to move off Looker or Power BI. It answers through them, so its numbers match theirs:


- **On Looker** , each question becomes an Explore query that Looker compiles from your LookML, with each Explore's default filters respected ([August 2026 release](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-08-01-answer-lineage) ) and row rules keyed on Looker user attributes. Details:[Looker integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) and our[Looker AI guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) .
- **On Power BI** , Dot reads each semantic model over XMLA and sends DAX that Power BI runs, so measures compute as they do in your reports. It needs Premium, Premium Per User or Fabric capacity, and can rebuild a report as a Dot dashboard checked visual by visual ([September 2026 release](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-09-01-train-dot) ). Details:[Power BI integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/power-bi) and our[Power BI Copilot guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/power-bi-copilot) .
- **If you run both,** Dot connects to each, plus warehouses like BigQuery and Postgres and semantic layers such as dbt, Cube and Malloy (45+ data sources in total), so one question in Slack is answered from whichever model owns the metric, with the LookML or DAX it ran shown alongside.


What it isn't: a pixel-perfect dashboard designer (keep your BI tool if hand-crafted reports are the main deliverable), and its business-app connectors such as HubSpot, Stripe and Google Ads are in beta. It's our product, so test it on your own data. Security details are on our[security page](https://www.getdot.ai/security) .


Dot bills on credits (usage), not seats, with unlimited users on every plan, so a Looker or Power BI estate with hundreds of occasional readers can get answers without buying more licenses.
